findings.title: Optimization removes the fail-closed contract
findings.evidence: The parser uses assert for ownership, duplicate keys, passed receipt, digest/argv/source membership and output checks, but does not refuse sys.flags.optimize or PYTHONOPTIMIZE before any file operation.
findings.required_change: Add an unconditional early optimized-mode refusal before reads/writes, or convert the safety predicates to explicit exceptions. Bind the exact interpreter/options in the admitted caller.

findings.title: Parsed snapshots can differ from the evidence digests
findings.evidence: plan, receipt, keeper and external are parsed from initial reads; keeper and receipt are hashed again later. A receipt or keeper A can be parsed while a subsequent read of B satisfies the external/keeper digest and is reported as its identity. The script also has no externally expected plan/external digest argument; those must be authenticated by an explicit exact immutable caller contract.
findings.required_change: Read each bound document once, calculate its digest and parse that same byte snapshot, compare those snapshot digests to externally frozen expected bindings, and report them. Retain any required pre/post path rechecks separately; do not substitute new reads for the snapshot identity.

findings.title: Input ownership is lexical and the reader is Linux-specific
findings.evidence: read_regular selects R/S with is_relative_to but never rejects parent components or checks resolved input containment. A lexical S/../outside/file can reach the root break in the ancestor loop while reading outside S. Separately, os.O_NOFOLLOW is a POSIX reader assumption and native Windows Python cannot be qualified by replacing root strings alone.
findings.required_change: Reject noncanonical/parent-traversal input paths and prove resolved containment plus existing no-link/type/identity checks. Declare the actual parser execution platform: retain a qualified POSIX reader for WSL or review a native Windows reparse/handle adaptation. Do not claim an output ../ bypass: line116 already rejects ordinary noncanonical/symlink output parents.

findings.title: Command environment is not closed over owned telemetry/cache helpers
findings.evidence: The env arrays set GOENV=off and selected compiler/cache/offline variables but inherit other ambient variables. In particular GOCACHEPROG and Go telemetry child controls are not cleared, and no task-owned TEST_TELEMETRY_DIR/off-mode binding is declared. The old draft cannot itself prove all Go helper/output effects remain under measured owned roots.
findings.required_change: Reuse the already qualified effective-environment and owned telemetry policy, explicitly remove external cache/telemetry child entrypoints, and freeze the owned off-mode bytes/path with the current target SDK provenance. This requires a narrow environment rebind, not a generic runner or SDK setup rewrite.

findings.title: Owned metadata fields are recorded without shape or location validation
findings.evidence: An owned ImportPath and any Dir value can satisfy the package-name set; file fields may be arbitrary truthy scalars instead of filename arrays. A matching name with a foreign Dir is recorded as an owned source package, so the parser does not itself establish the declared actual owned package/source inventory.
findings.required_change: Validate Dir as the expected current module/package directory, validate each source field as a bounded unique list of filenames and selection flags as their proper types, and retain the actual selected test-bearing set without promoting static declaration counts to actual cases. The admitted source/readset must bind these current directories/files.
